title: 49ers tabbed as a top fit for several players at key positions ahead of NFL trade deadline - NewsBreak
text:
By Mike Masala ,
3 hours ago Sep 8, 2024; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Dolphins linebacker Jaelan Phillips (15) celebrates after sacking Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (not pictured) during the fourth quarter at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images By Sam Navarro, Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The San Francisco 49ers have gone 5-2 through the first seven weeks of their 2025 campaign to position themselves in a three-way tie at the top of the NFC West with the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams.
However, San Francisco has also dealt with serious injuries to several key players, including Fred Warner and Nick Bosa, leaving them with some big holes to fill with backups and depth options on their own roster or practice squad.
With the NFL season halfway over, we're at the trade deadline, and many are wondering if the 49ers will pull the trigger and make a deal to improve their chances of making a run in the playoffs.
On Wednesday, ESPN's Matt Bowen and Jeremy Fowler released a list of the top 25 players that they believe could move. From that list of 25, they listed San Francisco as a top fit for seven of them.
Here's who they think could play well for the 49ers:
DE Trey Hendrickson, Bengals Hendrickson, 30, was a third-round pick (No. 103 overall) of the New Orleans Saints following a C-USA Defensive Player of the Year campaign at Florida Atlantic. After four years in New Orleans, he's spent the last four-plus years with the Cincinnati Bengals. In his NFL career, he's earned Pro Bowl honors four times and All-Pro honors once while recording 235 tackles (74 for a loss), 163 quarterback hits, 81 sacks, 16 passes defensed and 15 forced fumbles. However, he's dealing with a back injury and is on the final year of his rookie deal.
WR Chris Olave, Saints Olave, 25, played at Ohio State (2018-21) before the Saints took him in the first round (No. 11 overall) of the 2022 NFL draft. Since joining the Saints, he's caught 235 passes for 3,005 yards and 13 touchdowns. He's on pace to have one of the best seasons of his professional career, and he has one year left on his rookie deal.
EDGE Jaelan Phillips, Dolphins Phillips, 26, played at UCLA from 2017-18 and Miami (FL) from 2019-20 before joining the Miami Dolphins as a first-round pick in the 2021 NFL draft. Since, he's dealt with several injuries and has played in 53 games, recording 171 tackles (27 for a loss), 58 quarterback hits, 25 sacks, seven passes defensed, four fumbles recovered, one forced fumble and one interception. He'll be a free agent at the end of the year.
LB Logan Wilson, Bengals Wilson, 29, spent his college career at Wyoming (2015-19) before the Cincinnati Bengals took him in the third round (No. 65 overall) in the 2020 NFL draft. He's appeared in 75 games and recorded 536 tackles (19 tackles for a loss), 25 passes defensed, 18 quarterback hits, 11 interceptions, six forced fumbles, 5.5 sack and three fumble recoveries. He has two years remaining on his four-year, $36 million extension.
EDGE Arden Key, Titans Key, 29, played at LSU from 2015-17 and was drafted by the Raiders in 2018. He's also spent time with the 49ers, Jacksonville Jaguars and Tennessee Titans. In 109 career games, he's recorded 176 tackles (34 for a loss), 89 quarterback hits, 28 sacks, eight passes defensed, four forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries. His deal is set to void at the end of the 2025 season.
EDGE Kingsley Enagbare, Packers Enagbare, 25, was Green Bay's fifth-round pick (No. 179 overall) in the 2022 NFL draft out of South Carolina. Since then, he's appeared in 57 games and recorded 120 tackles (20 for a loss), 24 quarterback hits, 10 sacks, four passes defensed, three forced fumbles and one fumble recovery. He'll be a free agent this offseason.
LB Christian Harris, Texans Harris, 24, played at Alabama from 2019-21 before the Texans took him in the third round of the 2022 NFL draft. He's recorded 198 tackles (14 for a loss), 13 passes defensed, seven quarterback hits, four sacks, two forced fumbles and one interception. He'll be a free agent this offseason.
